content.intro: Learn Application Threat Modeling and Privacy through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding application threat modeling and privacy helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Application Threat Modeling and Privacy helps you reason about identifying assets and threats. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Identifying assets and threats. Then connect it to Least-privilege access. The remaining syllabus points—Safe logging and error messages, Secure defaults and incident response basics—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Application Threat Modeling and Privacy
content_blocks.code:
def valid_username?(value)
  value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(/\A[a-z0-9_]{3,20}\z/i)
end
puts valid_username?("learner_7")
puts valid_username?("bad name")

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports application threat modeling and privacy. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain application threat modeling and privacy, identify its place in ruby application security, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
